name: Cement
tile_text: Kiln and cooler castings, VRM rollers and table liners, mill liners and diaphragms.
desc: Wear- and heat-resistant castings for every stage of a cement plant: crushing, grinding, preheater, kiln and clinker cooler.
lede: Castings for every stage of the line, from the limestone crusher to the clinker cooler, each one chosen for the wear, impact and heat it will meet.
intro: A cement line asks two opposite things of its castings. At the front, parts must survive impact and abrasion at ambient temperature. From the preheater onwards, they must hold their shape and resist scaling in hot, corrosive gas. We pour both families, and we specify each part for the stage it works in.

steps.label: Crushing
steps.name: Crushing
steps.text: Limestone, shale and additives are broken down before grinding. The parts take repeated heavy impact, so toughness comes first and hardness second.
parts: Head wear, cracking at the pin bore
Edge wear, breakage on tramp metal

steps.label: Grinding
steps.name: Raw and cement grinding
steps.text: Vertical roller mills and ball mills grind raw meal, coal and cement. Wear here is mostly sliding abrasion, so the harder white irons earn their place.

steps.label: Preheater
steps.name: Preheater
steps.text: Raw meal meets hot kiln gas in the cyclone tower. Castings must keep their shape and resist oxidation and sulphur attack in the hottest stages.
parts: Splash boxes and meal distribution plates

steps.label: Kiln
steps.name: Kiln
steps.text: At the kiln inlet and outlet, castings hold refractory and seal the rotating shell. A failure here stops the whole plant, so we design for life between planned shutdowns.
parts: Tip castings and nose ring segments
Burn-off, cracking, loss of refractory hold

steps.label: Cooler
steps.name: Clinker cooler
steps.text: Grate plates carry and cool red-hot clinker under constant abrasion. The right alloy and a design that resists warping decide how long a grate lasts.

why: Both families, one foundry
Wear-resistant and heat-resistant alloys poured, treated and tested in the same plant.
Grade set by duty
We ask where the part runs and what it meets before we recommend a grade.
Ready for the shutdown
More than 10,000 patterns on file, and machining to 6,500 mm so parts fit first time.

name: Mining
tile_text: Crusher liners, mill liners and wear parts for primary and secondary crushing.
desc: Crusher liners, mill liners and material-handling wear parts for mines, cast in manganese steel, Cr-Mo steel and white irons.
lede: Wear parts for the crushers, mills and feeders that move ore from the pit to the plant.
intro: In a mine, a liner that fails early costs more in lost tonnes than the part itself. Primary crushers need tough steel that hardens under impact; mills need a balance of toughness and wear; feeders and conveyors need parts that take both. We cast for each duty and machine where the fit matters.

steps.label: Primary crushing
steps.name: Primary crushing
steps.text: Jaw and gyratory crushers take run-of-mine rock in heavy, repeated blows. Manganese steel is the standard here because its surface hardens as it is struck.
parts: Tooth wear, cracking, loss of nip

steps.label: Secondary crushing
steps.name: Secondary and tertiary crushing
steps.text: Cone crushers reduce ore to mill feed. Liner profile and alloy decide throughput and how often the crusher stops for a change.

steps.label: Grinding
steps.name: Grinding
steps.text: Ball and rod mills grind ore under combined impact and abrasion. Liners must lift the charge without breaking.

steps.label: Feeding and handling
steps.name: Feeding and handling
steps.text: Apron feeders, crawlers and conveyors carry rock between stages. Parts take impact from falling ore and wear from sliding.

why: Heavy pieces in one pour
Single castings up to 7 tonnes, with up to 10 tonnes of metal in one pour.
Toughness you can test
Impact and hardness tested on every heat, with reports traceable to the casting.
Machined to fit
Seats, bores and faces machined to drawing, up to 6,500 mm diameter.

name: Aggregate
tile_text: Jaw plates, concaves, mantles, blow bars and hammers for quarries.
desc: Crusher wear parts for quarries and aggregate producers: jaw plates, cone liners, blow bars and hammers.
lede: Crusher wear parts for quarries, where cost per tonne crushed is the number that matters.
intro: Quarries crush everything from soft limestone to abrasive granite. The same crusher needs a different liner for each, so we ask about the rock before we recommend the alloy and the profile.

steps.label: Jaw crushers
steps.name: Jaw crushers
steps.text: The primary crusher takes the largest rock. Jaw plates must stay tough while their teeth wear evenly.

steps.label: Cone crushers
steps.name: Cone crushers
steps.text: Secondary and tertiary cones shape the final product. Liner life and profile decide both cost and product size.

steps.label: Impact crushers
steps.name: Impact crushers
steps.text: Horizontal-shaft impactors throw rock against aprons at speed. Blow bars need hardness for wear and enough toughness to survive tramp metal.
parts: Cr-Mo steel, high chrome iron, manganese steel

why: Alloy matched to the rock
Limestone and granite need different liners; we ask before we quote.
Patterns on file
More than 10,000 patterns, so common crusher models are ready to cast.
Shipped anywhere
Packed and documented for export to plants anywhere in the world.

name: Steel and power
tile_text: Coal mill and crusher parts for power plants, and heat-resistant castings for steel plants.
desc: Coal mill and coal crusher wear parts for thermal power plants, and heat-resistant castings for steel plants and furnaces.
lede: Coal mill and crusher parts for power stations, and heat-resistant castings for furnaces and pellet plants.
intro: Thermal power plants wear out their coal crushers and mills; steel plants burn through the castings inside their furnaces and pellet lines. One needs abrasion resistance, the other strength at heat. We pour both.

steps.label: Coal crushing
steps.name: Coal crushing
steps.text: Ring granulators and hammer crushers size coal before the mills. Parts take impact and abrasive wear from coal and stones.

steps.label: Coal grinding
steps.name: Coal grinding
steps.text: Vertical and tube mills grind coal to fine powder for the boiler. Sliding abrasion dominates, so white irons last longest.

steps.label: Furnaces and pellets
steps.name: Furnaces and pellet plants
steps.text: Inside furnaces and on travelling grates, castings must carry load at high temperature without scaling or creeping out of shape.

why_title: Why steel and power plants choose us
why: Wear and heat in one plant
Abrasion-resistant irons and heat-resistant steels under one roof.
Tested before it ships
Chemistry, hardness and NDT reported for every heat.
Ready for outages
Patterns on file and machining in-house to meet planned shutdowns.

name: Equipment makers
tile_text: Castings machined to drawing for crusher, mill and kiln manufacturers.
desc: Castings and machined components to drawing for crusher, mill, kiln and process equipment manufacturers.
lede: Castings and machined components made to your drawing, for the equipment you build and service.
intro: Original equipment makers need a foundry that works to their drawing, their standard and their schedule. We review the drawing, design the method, cast, heat treat and machine, and send the reports your quality team needs.

steps.label: Drawing review
steps.name: Drawing review and method
steps.text: Our engineers review the drawing for castability and agree the method, the grade and the inspection plan before a pattern is made.
parts: Avoids hot spots, shrinkage and costly rework
Checks feeding before metal is poured
Sets what is tested and reported

steps.label: First article
steps.name: Pattern and first article
steps.text: Patterns are made in-house. The first casting is fully inspected and reported before series production starts.
parts: Series production starts on your sign-off

steps.label: Series production
steps.name: Series production and machining
steps.text: Castings are poured, heat treated and machined to drawing, with each one traceable to its heat.
parts: Turned and bored up to 6,500 mm

why: Your drawing, your standard
IS, ASTM or your own specification, with an agreed inspection plan.
From 3 kg to 7 tonnes
Small series and heavy single pieces from the same foundry.
Cast and machined
One supplier for the casting and the machined part.
